recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future work should be a separate editorial cleanup only if the work group wants to polish the existing wording; the substantive FHIR-31817 clarification is already in build-scoped source.
issue_request: FHIR-31817 asked BR&R to improve documentation because the MedicinalProductIngredient definitions did not clearly explain what units of presentation are. Jira is Published with resolution Persuasive, vote 10-0-0, applied for R5, and a comment says the change was applied.
initial_application: The old MedicinalProductIngredient artifact is redirected to Ingredient in source/fhir.ini. History shows explicit non-ancestor commit 72c7bcfe69 adding the current unit-of-presentation sentence for FHIR#31817, and current ancestor commit 464b98e6e7 carries that same clarification into the branch where git blame now attributes the line.
additional_context: Ingredient is an active draft resource in the current build, while MedicinalProductIngredient is a redirect to Ingredient. Later Published issue FHIR-39134 discussed concentration and presentation strength and asked for examples; its comments support the existing distinction between presentation strength as per-item or consumer-facing expression and concentration strength as normalized calculation, and do not reverse FHIR-31817.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/ingredient/structuredefinition-Ingredient.xml already explains Ingredient.substance.strength.presentation[x] as the quantity of substance in the unit of presentation and clarifies that this is the quantity the item occurs in, for example a strength per tablet size rather than a normalized unitary denominator. The Ingredient example also distinguishes presentation per item from concentration per unit of measure.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Ingredient issue discussed concentration and presentation strength and resulted in examples/comments that support the current distinction.
Earlier Published Ingredient strength issue established the choice-type shape of presentation/concentration strength that FHIR-31817 later clarified.
